root_idea.summary: The root centers on being struck by scorching heat, especially when the face or surface is visibly affected.
root_idea.development: The core thermal sense extends to fire, sun, and hot wind. A light sword blow is recorded as a secondary or metaphorical application, with its original basis questioned in favor of نفح.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized perfect Form I citation form لَفَحَ rather than the attested imperfect تَلْفَحُ.

senses.definition: To strike and scorch with intense heat; to burn.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction, fire is the agent and faces are the object: the fire scorches their faces. The form is attested as the active imperfect تَلْفَحُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strike someone lightly or slightly with a sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with بِالسَّيْفِ; the blow is explicitly characterized as light or slight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A light or slight blow with a sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for the corresponding slight sword stroke.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A blast or gust of heat, especially a burning hot wind such as ḥarūr or samūm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used for a hot blast or burning gust; the contrast with نفح concerns a cold or cool wind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A well-known yellow, sweet-scented plant of the yَقْطِينِيّ kind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plant is described as one that people smell for its sweet odor and as resembling a yellowing eggplant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The fruit or produce of the mandrake.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical application of the same term to the mandrake’s fruit or produce.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Thermal striking or burning by fire and hot wind is represented by the thermal sense.
Light sword striking is represented as a separate classical construction.
The noun for a burning gust is represented.
The heat-versus-cold wind contrast is covered by the hot-gust meaning.
The plural application remains the same hot-gust meaning.
The noun for a slight sword blow is represented.
The plant sense is represented under the normalized لُفَّاحٌ spelling.
The mandrake-fruit application is represented separately.

cautions: The botanical Lane entry is headed in the extracted data as لُقَّاحٌ, while its body identifies the term as لُفَّاحٌ and discusses meanings consistent with that spelling; the public headword is normalized to لُفَّاحٌ based on the body and root context.
